headline: Marvel Television Announces New Animated Projects and Live-Action Series at New York Comic-Con

sources.excerpt: There are some new animated projects coming from Marvel Television, per the studio’s New York Comic-Con panel on Thursday. Marvel Zombies is returning for the first of three all-new Halloween specials next year. In 2027, fans can expect Marvel Zombies: The Winter Soldier, followed by The Fist of Khonshu and The Last Guardian. The animated project began last year as a four-episode series in which a slew of MCU actors lent their voices to their respective roles, including Elizabeth Olsen, Paul Rudd, Florence Pugh, David Harbour, Tessa Thompson, Simu Liu, Awkwafina, Hailee Steinfeld, Wyatt Russell, Randall Park, Iman Vellani and Dominique Thorne. The series also brought The Blade to the MCU, voiced by Todd Williams. In Marvel Zombies, after the Avengers are overtaken by a zombie plague, a desperate group of survivors discover the key to bringing an end to the super-powered undead, racing across a dystopian landscape and risking life and limb to save their world. Marvel Zombies was created by Bryan Andrews and Zeb Wells. The series is executive produced by Kevin Feige, Louis D’Esposito, Brad Winderbaum, Dana Vasquez-Eberhardt, Bryan Andrews and Zeb Wells, and is produced by Danielle Costa, Carrie Wassenaar. Also, Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man is swinging its way back onto Disney+ in the new year. Season 2 is set to premiere on January 13, 2027, the studio says. The first 10-episode season of Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man hit the streamer last year. The voice cast includes Hudson Thames as Peter Parker as well as Colman Domingo, Eugene Byrd, Grace Song, Zeno Robinson, Hugh Dancy and Charlie Cox. Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man follows Peter Parker on his way to becoming Spider-Man in the MCU. In this alternate timeline, as the clip previews, the webslinger’s origin story features a mentorship by Norman Osborn (of Oscorp fame), the alter ego to bitter enemy Green Goblin, instead of Tony Stark.

Marvel Television revealed the first logo for its new series “Zodiac,” a live-action spy thriller set for release in 2028. The series will begin shooting in London in the spring, Marvel Television chief Brad Winderbaum said during its New York Comic-Con panel, with casting beginning in the “next couple of weeks.” No additional details were immediately available. “Zodiac” marks the first new live-action show that’s been announced for Marvel since last year’s “Ironheart.” While the MCU had a massive hit on the big-screen with “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” breaking records at the box office, the TV universe had some popular shows come to an end. Just a few months after it premiered in January, “Wonder Man” was canceled — despite being renewed for a second season and landing an Emmy nomination for lead actor Yahya Abdul-Mateen II. The show was critically acclaimed, and it made Abdul-Mateen II the first live-action actor to receive an Emmy nod for both a Marvel and DC series after he starred in HBO’s “Watchmen.” Then, it was revealed that “Daredevil: Born Again” would end with next year’s Season 3. The series revived Charlie Cox’s popular street-level hero after he debuted in Netflix’s “Daredevil” show. Season 3 looks to be a long-awaited reunion for the Netflix “Defenders” heroes, including Krysten Ritter as Jessica Jones, Mike Colter as Luke Cage and Finn Jones as Iron First. “VisionQuest” is set to premiere on Oct. 14 and will cap off the trilogy of shows that began with “WandaVision” and then “Agatha All Along.” After starring in “WandaVision,” Paul Bettany is back as the robot Vision, who’s been hiding out and communicating with other AI androids brought to life, like Ultron, J.A.R.V.I.S., F.R.I.D.A.Y. and more.
